surfaces.density: Inconsistent. observations.claim: Sign-out uses Color(0xFFDC2626), a fourth distinct red in this cluster and not the design-system error token #D73C3C; it is a literal so it does not adapt in dark theme.
Every icon on the screen has contentDescription = null, including the actionable sign-out affordance, so screen-reader users get an unlabelled control.
The AuthState.Initializing case is unhandled — the screen renders 'Guest' with a '?' avatar during session restore instead of a skeleton, so cold-start shows wrong identity data.
The support phone number is hardcoded in the composable rather than a string/config resource, and the display form '1800-123-456' does not match the dialled form 'tel:1800123456'.
Four raw sp values (24sp avatar initials, 20sp name override, 15sp labels x2) bypass the mapped typography scale entirely.

Flat-gray-card syndrome: all three SectionCards and the sign-out card use the identical surface fill + 1dp outline + 12dp radius, so a destructive action is visually near-identical to 'Booking history'.

Two near-duplicate privacy entries sit adjacent in the Support section — 'Manage privacy' (consent screen) and 'Privacy and data' (the privacy hub that itself contains consent) — plus a third 'Privacy policy' dialog, giving three shield-icon rows in a row.
Name edit and sign-out produce zero feedback: no snackbar, no progress, no error path; ProfileViewModel launches both without observing the result.
The screen has no title and no back/close affordance of its own; the only heading semantics are attached to the user's name.
0.5dp dividers will round to a sub-pixel hairline on low-density screens common in this rural market segment.

observations.claim: The entire screen is unreachable — no composable() registers LocaleRoutes.DATA_EXPORT and the only entry point passes onDownloadData = null.

None of the nine data_export_* strings have Hindi translations, so the screen is English-only in a bilingual app (en file has them at values/strings.xml:382-390; values-hi/strings.xml contains no data_export_* key).
Loading is a bare centred CircularProgressIndicator, and the identical indicator is reused for Loading, Ready and Saved so three semantically different states are visually identical.
Error rendering discards DataExportUiState.Error.message and always prints the same generic sentence, collapsing network, auth and storage failures into one indistinguishable panel.
The error panel colours are three fixed light hex literals with no dark-theme variant, so the panel stays pink-on-pink over a near-black background.
The string 'Download my data' appears three times on one screen — as the screen title, the hero card title, and the CTA label.
SAF cancel silently resets to Idle with no message, so a user who backs out of the file picker sees the screen revert with no explanation.

The export filename timestamp is formatted with Locale.US, which is correct for filesystem safety but means the file name is never localized while the prefix string is a translatable resource — an inconsistency.

observations.claim: The countdown string is built in English in Kotlin with English pluralization ('days'/'hours'), so Hindi users see English on the most consequential screen in the app.
The translated framing string delete_account_coolOff_countdown_format exists in both locales but is never used — the bare fragment is rendered with no surrounding sentence.

observations.claim: formatCountdown returns an empty string on parse failure or a past target date, and the else branch renders that empty string with no fallback, producing a countdown card containing an hourglass and a blank line.

The SnackbarHost is a second direct child of Surface alongside the Column; Material3 Surface stacks its children in a propagate-min-constraints Box, so the snackbar renders overlapping the top bar rather than at the bottom.
Revoke-failure snackbars carry raw exception text from the ViewModel.

The revoked success banner is dead UI — the Revoked state simultaneously triggers navigation away, so the confirmation is drawn for one frame at most and the user lands on Settings with no acknowledgement.

The countdown icon is triple-nested — a 64dp Box wrapping a Surface wrapping another 64dp Box — so the 12%-alpha chip fills the outer box exactly and the visual is indistinguishable from a single Surface.
The countdown card uses a 24dp radius while every other card in the same three-screen flow uses 20dp, so the flow's corner language is inconsistent within itself.
The countdown value updates every 60 seconds with no liveRegion semantics and no animation, so neither sighted nor screen-reader users perceive the change.
